data_flow: Approved provider -> existing identity/authorization gateway -> scoped retrieval -> minimization and encrypted bounded cache.
Normalized authorized records -> deterministic academic services -> privacy/content/recipient recheck -> permitted MCP response.
Permitted document bytes -> isolated bounded worker -> restricted text or pixels -> purpose and modality checks before release.
Local console explicit material -> local-only document adapter; fictional demo -> offline grade calculation. Neither needs LMS credentials.
Retention and revocation fence credentials, cached records, jobs and temporary links; downstream copies remain controlled by their own services.
Governance command reads public repository metadata and sanitized outcome receipts only; it does not inspect live configuration or private evidence.
Approved normalized input -> operation-bound receipt -> host-minimized numeric projection -> bounded declarative module -> renewed policy check and original provenance/restrictions.
limitations: All external permissions remain independently established; the register is not runtime authorization.
Automated privacy and fixture screens cannot prove absence of all personal data; repository-content review remains mandatory.
Unsigned developer receipts require verification against trusted CI provenance or supervised reproduction.
The project has not adopted an open-source license. Repository visibility grants no license.
OS-specific workers, optional native converters, operational readiness and deployed platform behavior require their own evidence.
Policy sources are a reviewed subset; institution-specific contracts and legal applicability require authorized review.
A stale, missing, failed or skipped required check cannot be converted to success by a report flag.
SDK v1 supports a points-based aggregate scenario and bounded declarative modules only. New providers, projections and native-code execution are not enabled by capability discovery.
